title: Streams Simulator Run Artifact v0.1
description: The single file that reproduces a run. This is the deterministic-simulation-testing contract: if a failure cannot be reduced to one of these, it is not reproducible and the architecture is wrong. `streamsim replay` consumes it with no MCP server running, which is what turns an improvised exploratory session into a committed regression fixture.

sim_version.description: Part of the determinism tuple. A different simulator version may legitimately produce a different trace; verify reports that as a version mismatch rather than a failure.

created_at.description: Wall clock, for humans. Never an input to anything.

digest.description: RFC 8785 canonical digest of the normalized domain spec.

sink.description: Where rendered records were delivered. MCP manages the simulator and never carries evidence, so there is no MCP sink. broker is deferred and fails at load with not_implemented.

adapter.description: Which output adapter rendered the run. Part of the determinism tuple: the same world under two adapters produces two different byte streams, both correct.

world_digest.description: Digest over (sim_version, domain digest, seed, world_config). Two creates with the same arguments must agree; a divergence means the environment changed and the runs are not comparable.

command_log.description: Every mutation, in a total order established under the world mutex before seq assignment — so concurrent MCP calls cannot reorder it. Replaying this log, not re-issuing the MCP calls, is what reproduces the run.

at_ns.description: World clock at which the command applied. Never a wall-clock read.

op.description: Names match the MCP_SURFACE tools minus the 'sim.' prefix. env has no clear: pause and kill are momentary.

args.description: Canonical arguments, RFC 8785 normalized before hashing.

expected_trace_digest.description: Digest of the emitted trace. `verify` regenerates and compares; on mismatch it reports the first divergent record index rather than a bare boolean.

reproducible.description: False for http-push + wall, where delivery timing comes from a real clock and cannot be reproduced, and for any closed-loop run where the consumer did not report quiescence. Scorecards refuse to report hash-equality metrics for a run with this false, and every report carries the flag.

unblinded.description: Set permanently and irreversibly when truth.reveal was called with unblind:true on an open run. An unblinded run is excluded from every scorecard and the exclusion count is printed.

platform.description: Recorded so that a cross-architecture digest divergence is diagnosable rather than mysterious. Not part of the determinism tuple: identical output across platforms is a requirement, not a variable.
